children: Australian shares rebounded from a one-month low on Thursday, led by heavyweight banks, as easing oil prices and bond yields lifted global risk sentiment while investors looked past expectations of further domestic monetary tightening.

Sydney's rebound tracked gains in global markets as bond yields and oil prices fell, easing concerns over borrowing costs and geopolitical risks.[MKTS/GLOB]

The improved global mood lifted Australian equities, while upbeat June-quarter GDP data strengthened the case for further monetary tightening and bolstered expectations of another Reserve Bank of Australia rate hike.

Hersh Oberoi, global research director at Balfour Capital, however cautioned that the day's move looks more like a relief rally than a meaningful shift in risk appetite adding the pressures that had been driving the market lower have simply stopped intensifying.
"Materials was comfortably the worst-performing sector yesterday, which makes it the most obvious candidate for a bounce. This looks like positioning rather than conviction," added Oberoi.
